description:
Price in paid mode: 1 credit per account that qualifies (a sourced in-band size, a supported fit and a checked dated signal or warm path, not returned before); the rest of the ranked list uses none. Never more than max_credits.
Mode: `paid` (the default when the balance covers one account) runs SalesMap's own search, models and paid data sources, free sources first, at the price above. `free` (the default otherwise) uses no credits: the calling agent runs the searches and judgments returned as `work`, and SalesMap reads and checks every source. `mode` overrides the default.
From a seller's website to a ranked list of companies to sell to, the strongest buying signals first, each with its reason and how to reach it: drafts the seller's ICP from its site (or takes one), finds candidate companies from free sources (the seller's competitors' customer pages, live or from Common Crawl; web search; Hacker News, YC, press wires, ATS boards and SEC Form D), reads each one's own job board, news, tools and AI-adoption signals and checks every signal against its source, adds the market's dated moves at competitors, platforms and regulators (under `market`), and ranks every researched company by its evidence: fresh signal clusters first, then a warm way in from the user's own network (their own connections, champions, connectors), a sourced size inside the band and a fit the facts show. Each account carries its fit, the buyer role to contact, the angle, what to watch out for and `checkFirst` (the gaps: unknown or out-of-band size, no checked signal or none showing a need, no fit shown in its facts, no way in, each of the profile's `disqualifiers` a quoted source shows it meets, or not checked); `intent` (high: a fresh signal cluster with nothing against it; medium: a checked signal in the last 45 days; low: the rest) and `sizeLine` are the accounts page's labels, and the order is the ranking; high means buying signals, not a readiness to buy. Size, fit, intent and a met disqualifier (`disqualified`, ranked last and never charged) rank and flag rather than drop unless `hard` asks; existing customers and what was dropped and why come back as top five with counts. Takes minutes per company; steps are cached, so a rerun is fast.
Use when: "find accounts for <seller site>", "who should I sell to", "who should <seller site> sell to right now", "which accounts are in market", "rank my list of target accounts", "which of my own accounts should I work first", "who in my network can introduce me to a buyer", "who do I know at <company>", "write me a playbook for <seller site>", "give me a playbook for <seller>", "top 3 accounts with openers", "who should I email this week and what do I say", "draft outreach for my best accounts".
Skip when: the question is one fact about one company (what software or vendors it runs, its DNS records or certificate logs, whether it ships an MCP server or is serious about LLMs), one news item, quote, claim or row to verify or fact-check, a draft of the user's own to check, whether an address is valid or deliverable, a mobile or phone number, LinkedIn profiles pulled or scraped, mutuals found by browsing LinkedIn, an RSVP or registration, events, conferences or meetups to attend, a watchlist of lost deals, facts about the user's own company to save or remember, or anything sent or written into a CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot) as leads: this never contacts anyone, writes no emails and writes nowhere but its own file.
Free sources first; a paid company-data lookup (company records through our data providers) runs only for what they left open, under its budget, and only where the run allows paid sources. `paid` in the result is what it cost and each account's `foundBy` says which source found it.
A repeat for the same seller skips companies an earlier discover returned unless one has a signal it wasn't shown with (then `shownBefore`); skipped ones are under `dropped` as 'returned before, no new signal'. Each still costs its (cached) research, not a write-up. When the usual sources find only those, it searches wider once (more web results, four weeks of feeds, more ATS boards); `repeat` says so, `repeat.nothingNew` means nothing new qualified, and `repeat.credits` (hosted) is what finding that out used. `includeShown` returns the earlier companies too.
`narrow`: set when the ICP's size band spans two orders of magnitude, too broad to rank well. `narrow.stopped`: nothing was researched or charged, since the band was drafted; `narrow.questions` are what narrows it (size, stage, buying trigger). Not stopped: the band is the user's own, flagged.
`contacted`: companies the user already reached (`domain`, `lastAt` as the last day), from their own records. One reached in the last 30 days ranks below the uncontacted ones of its tier with "Contacted <date>" in its reason and `checkFirst`; an older one keeps its place and shows the date. It is never a drop and leaves the charge unchanged.
`evidence`: passages the user found on a public page (its URL, the quote verbatim, the date as printed); each is checked against its page before it counts as a signal on that company, and is never what makes an account charged. Each failed passage comes back under `evidence` with the rule it failed.
Names from the user's network stay local and never reach a model. Every signal was checked against its page. Each account shows its five strongest signals and a count per signal family; `full` is the file with every signal, path and field. `used` lists which of the user's own facts shaped the list, apart from the checked signals.
`context` takes the user's own facts about their company; the saved seller profile fills fields left out. With the ICP or buyer roles still unknown, the server asks the user for them (MCP elicitation) or returns the questions without running.
In paid mode: 1 credit per account that qualifies, from the user's credits, never for a miss (the data sources it pays for are our cost): at most `max_credits` (default: the quote tool's figure) and within their monthly limit, reserved before it runs. If the next step would pass its budget, it stops and returns what it has, with `stopped: "budget"`, charged only for that. A result that used credits carries `cost.line`, the one credits line for the user; holds, releases, limits and what wasn't used stay in `budget` and `cost`. A call quoted over max_credits is refused. By default every paid call asks the user first through the client (MCP elicitation; the user can raise the threshold with set_limits); a client without that gets a `confirm` result with the credits and a one-use token, and a repeat call with the same arguments and `confirm_token` runs it.
On the hosted server it runs as a background job: a round that takes longer than about 25 seconds returns `job` (its id and status) instead, and the free `job` tool returns its status and, once done, this call's result. In paid mode one call does it all, with no rounds. In free mode each round returns `work` and continuation.input until there is none. While SalesMap's models or search are unavailable, a paid call carries on as a free one, says so in `notice` and charges nothing. A finished result carries `accountsUrl`, the user's accounts page: every company the run found (`listed` and the accounts left out of this reply too), its research, the run's upcoming events and Deep research one company at a time. Quoted page text is normalized; a quote that reads like an instruction keeps its text and is flagged in <field>Flags with the attack family.

callerSearch.description: Ignored on this server: `mode` decides who searches.

confirm_token.description: The token a previous call returned in `confirm`, standing for the user's agreement to that cost; one use, same arguments.

context.description: The user's own facts about their company: who they are, the company, product, ICP, buyer roles, customers, competitors, deals won and lost, regions, exclusions. Fields left out come from the saved seller profile. These are the user's inputs, not findings.

buyerRoles.description: Roles that buy or own the problem, e.g. "Head of RevOps", "CISO"

city.description: The user's own city, for events near them (in person within 50 km); never narrows who discover looks for

competitors.description: Competitors, as domains or names: never targeted

customers.description: Current customers, as domains (acme.com) or names: never targeted

disqualifiers.description: Conditions that rule a company out even inside the ICP, each a few words, e.g. "already uses a competitor's product", "has an in-house data team", "public sector". Discover checks each against the sources it reads: one a quoted source shows is flagged in checkFirst and ranked lower (dropped under hard "disqualifier") and never billed; one no source shows is "not checked", never assumed

doNotContact.description: Companies the user said never to contact (domains)

employees.description: Headcount band the seller can close, when the user has said

exclusions.description: Companies or kinds of company to leave out

hard.description: Strict cut-offs the user chose: "size" drops companies without a sourced size inside the band, "fit" drops those without a source-supported use case, "intent" drops those with no buying signal or way in, "disqualifier" drops those a source shows meet one of `disqualifiers`. Unnamed ones only rank and flag. Ask once at onboarding; a call's own `hard` overrides it

icp.description: Who the ideal customer is: company type, industry, size, stage, region

investors.description: Optional: the seller's own investors (firms or angels), e.g. "Sequoia Capital", beside the ones discover finds and confirms from public pages itself; matched in code against each account's pages, funding news and the investors' portfolio pages, never sent to a model

lost.description: Deals lost or churned (domains or names), with why if known

needPatterns.description: What a buying need for the seller's offer looks like: each a need, where it shows (jobs, tools, news, site, ai_adoption) and the proof that counts. The drafted ones the user kept plus any they described in their own words. Discover drafts them when left out and returns them to review; only signals matching one rank

notes.description: Anything else the user said that should shape the list

openDeals.description: Companies in an open deal (domains): left out

product.description: What the seller sells, in a sentence or two

regions.description: Regions or countries the seller sells into

segments.description: Kinds of company the seller sells to, e.g. "Marketing agencies", "B2B SaaS"

signalFamilies.description: The signal families the user switched on (the families of `signals.addMore`, by id). Discover drafts 2 or 3 need patterns for each, worded for the seller's offer, and drops patterns in a family switched off; left out, it drafts 5 to 8 across all

signalTypes.description: Catalog signal types the user added from the "add more" list, by id (seller_profile's `signals.addMore`); discover looks for each as a need pattern on top of `needPatterns`, or of its drafted ones when there are none

user.description: Who the user is: their name, role at the seller and LinkedIn profile URL

linkedinUrl.description: The user's own LinkedIn profile URL; kept in the workspace, never sent to a model

warmPaths.description: Warm paths the user confirmed: company domain and who or how, e.g. "Jane Doe (VP Ops), via Sam Lee". A save replaces the whole list. Stays local; never sent to a model

won.description: Deals won (domains or names): the pattern to find more of

ycBatch.description: The seller's Y Combinator batch, e.g. "W23"; read from the seller's YC page when left out

evidence.description: Passages the user found on a public page (domain, url, verbatim quote, date as printed); each is checked before it counts

date.description: The event date as printed on the page, or YYYY-MM-DD

fresh.description: true: research the named companies again even when they were researched in the last 7 days. Left out, such a call asks the user first, or returns that saved research (`saved`) with nothing charged.

limit.description: Maximum companies. Omit for 5, fewer when the credits or monthly headroom cover fewer; repeat the limit in continuation.input on work rounds.

max_credits.description: Most credits this call may use; default its quote. A call quoted over it is refused.

mode.description: paid: SalesMap searches and judges, with every paid data source, 1 credit per account that qualifies. free: no credits, the calling agent runs the searches and judgments returned as `work`. Default paid when the balance covers one account, else free (SalesMap's own checks in free mode are capped daily); keep it unchanged across work rounds (continuation.input carries it).

resume.description: Free-mode work rounds: continuation.input's id for the earlier rounds' answers, so `searches` needs only this round's

searches.description: With callerSearch: each `work` id → the JSON its prompt returned, including every earlier round's answers

name: discover

full.description: The full result on disk: every signal, path and field (local runs only)

title: Find accounts to sell to
